review.causal_identification_assessment: Option B provides the strongest causal identification because MRW and WIN-C are generated from the same frozen initial skill, exact pools, updater configuration, executor, held-out probes, renderer, and budgets, with update and evaluation order interleaved/hash-balanced in the same post-gate tranche. This makes the paired contrast J_s(MRW)-J_s(WIN-C) interpretable as the effect of the mixed-rejected-witness projection under shared contemporaneous hosted-provider conditions. Option A remains interpretable only under an additional no-material-drift assumption between the WIN-A/WIN-B collection window and the later MRW window; the negative-control equivalence gate qualifies WIN-A versus WIN-B but cannot certify that future MRW calls occur under unchanged service conditions.
review.cost_benefit_assessment: Option B adds approximately 12 learned winner-control states and 12 additional 18-probe K=1 evaluations, doubling post-gate learned-state execution from 12 to 24. That cost is material but modest relative to the inferential risk of having the entire treatment arm collected in a later hosted-service tranche than the control arm. Because the MRW experiment is the central causal claim, the additional WIN-C run is justified by substantially improved reviewer robustness and a cleaner estimand; Option A's savings do not compensate for the avoidable drift objection.
review.historical_control_usage: WIN-A/WIN-B should not be pooled into the primary control if Option B is adopted. Their equivalence-gated role is to validate the stability of the identical-treatment winner-control pipeline and to serve as secondary bridge/stability evidence connecting the fresh WIN-C tranche to the earlier V3.1 winner-evidence runs. They may be reported descriptively and used in sensitivity analyses, but the primary causal contrast must remain MRW versus contemporaneous WIN-C.
nonblocking_notes: If Option A had been forced by budget, the preregistered mean of WIN-A/WIN-B would be preferable to WIN-A alone because it preserves the same winner-only estimand while reducing control-side sampling noise; averaging identical-treatment replicates changes the control estimator's precision, not the target estimand.
Option B should still report a bridge comparison among WIN-A, WIN-B, and WIN-C to characterize tranche stability, but that comparison must not alter the primary MRW versus WIN-C contrast.
All claims should remain limited to the frozen streams, tasks, probes, model, renderer, updater, and budgets; no generalization beyond the measured paired projection effect is authorized.
review.primary_decision_rule: Before any MRW outcomes exist, freeze a one-sided confirmatory paired test of H0: Delta <= 0 versus H1: Delta > 0 at alpha = 0.05, using a preregistered paired permutation or paired t procedure across the 12 stream-level D_s values with the exact multiple-comparison/error-control rule fixed in advance. STOP for the confirmatory claim if the preregistered test does not reject H0 or if any frozen validity gate fails; HOLD if execution, provenance, balancing, renderer, probe, or budget integrity is incomplete or adjudication is not blinded. A positive result supports only the paired contemporaneous projection effect and does not authorize broader paper claims beyond that estimand.
review.primary_estimand: For each stream s, freeze D_s = J_s(MRW_s) - J_s(WIN-C_s), where J_s is the fixed held-out 18-probe K=1 evaluation score under the frozen renderer and budgets. The primary estimand is the mean paired effect across the 12 frozen streams, Delta = (1/12) * sum_s D_s, equivalently the stream-level average treatment effect of the mixed-rejected-witness projection relative to a contemporaneous winner-only control under the same initial skill, exact pools, updater implementation/configuration, executor, probes, renderer, and budgets.

remaining_blockers.exact_repair: Do not create, execute, score, or inspect MRW until the frozen WIN-A/WIN-B equivalence gate is formally recorded as PASS under the preregistered margin; if it fails, stop MRW permanently for this design cycle.
remaining_blockers.issue: The negative-control equivalence gate has not yet been adjudicated, so MRW remains unauthorized.

remaining_blockers.exact_repair: Before execution, freeze the hash seed, interleaving schedule, update-order balancing, held-out evaluation-order balancing, retry policy, timeout policy, and provenance logging for WIN-C versus MRW across all 12 streams.
remaining_blockers.issue: Option B requires a frozen contemporaneous execution protocol so that WIN-C and MRW are actually paired rather than merely collected nearby in time.

remaining_blockers.exact_repair: Preregister the exact paired test, alpha, one-sided hypothesis, handling of failed or invalid streams, missing-data rule, and STOP/HOLD adjudication criteria before any WIN-C or MRW score is opened.
remaining_blockers.issue: The primary inferential rule must be fixed before MRW outcomes exist to avoid analytic degrees of freedom.

remaining_blockers.exact_repair: Label WIN-A/WIN-B in the analysis plan as secondary bridge/stability evidence only, with any pooling or cross-tranche sensitivity analysis explicitly non-confirmatory.
remaining_blockers.issue: Historical WIN-A/WIN-B could be misused as an additional primary control after results are known.

review.single_sentence_recommendation: Conditional only on a preregistered negative-control equivalence PASS, choose Option B and freeze MRW versus contemporaneous WIN-C as the sole primary paired control, with WIN-A/WIN-B retained strictly as secondary bridge and stability evidence.
review.temporal_drift_assessment: Hosted-provider temporal drift is a material confound even when the resolved model ID is unchanged, because routing, infrastructure, safety layers, decoding behavior, latency-dependent truncation, evaluator availability, and other hidden service updates can shift outcomes. The drift risk is asymmetric in Option A: all control observations precede all MRW observations, so any monotone or tranche-level service change is aliased directly with the projection treatment. Option B does not eliminate drift, but interleaving and hash-balancing convert much of the tranche-level drift into shared nuisance variation rather than a systematic treatment-control difference.
